l-001.evidence: The one readable query (seq 1) returns 6 rows, all with falco.output_fields.user.name=root, proc.pname=bash, proc.name/uid/tty null, and cmdline drawn from exactly the same three-command set seen in every control — "sudo -n systemctl status elastic-agent", "sudo -n journalctl -u elastic-agent -n 10", "sudo -n ss -tnlp" — emitted as two same-millisecond triads at 06:41:01 and 06:41:41. The live controls carry the identical triad with identical user/pname/cmdline values: C-21d 3 rows, C-35d 10 rows, C-28d 13 rows including near-adjacent bursts at 06:33:48 and 06:34:07 (19 s apart), so neither the command set nor the burst cadence is new, and 6 rows over 15 minutes is not above the 3–13 rows/hour control range. The only column that could separate observed from baseline is falco.output_fields.container.id (ed96a85a7480, matching most baseline rows anyway), and environment_notes lists that column as an unstable identifier that cannot evidence a delta. Seq 0 is unreadable, but it differs from seq 1 only by adding proc.loginuid, and seq 1 alone settles the lead.

l-002.evidence: Both queries in this lead are cmdb templates (cmdb.host-trust-edges, cmdb.list-all-hosts), and environment_notes states cmdb returns current configuration or an entity record with no @timestamp bounds to move, hence no control and no baseline-diff semantics — consistent with the empty `baseline` array. The one readable payload (seq 1) is an inventory listing with total: 11 and hosts canary-1, ci-1, config-mgmt-1, db-1, dev-ws-1, jump-box-1, office-ws-1, office-ws-2, scanner-1, web-1, web-2, each carrying role/criticality/owner/trust_edges_out/users fields; soc-playground does not appear among them. The seq 0 host-scoped payload is unreadable, but that does not change the classification: state-only applies regardless of whether rows changed, so only one decidable query exists and heterogeneity is null.

l-003.evidence: The lead contains a single query, `change-mgmt.active-changes`, parameterised by host `soc-playground` and instant `2026-07-28T06:45:14Z`. The environment notes state explicitly that change-mgmt queries return current configuration or an entity record rather than an event stream, carry no `@timestamp` bounds to move, and therefore have no control and no baseline-diff semantics. The observed payload is an empty list (zero CR rows, so no CR id, status, window_start/window_end, host scope, requester, or CHG-RUNNER prefix to report) and the baseline is likewise empty, but per the rules that changed-or-unchanged distinction is irrelevant for a state/lookup system. Tagged `state-only` regardless of row content; `heterogeneous` is null because fewer than two decidable queries exist.

l-004.evidence:
All nine queries in this lead are ticket lookups (status/keyword filters such as
status=open, status=in_progress, q=soc-playground, q=sudo, q=keycloak, q=credential
stuffing, and an unfiltered ticket.all-tickets) against the ticketing/change-management
system, which returns ticket records rather than a timestamped event stream. Every
observed payload is `total: 0` with `tickets: []`, and the `baseline` array is empty
because these queries carry no `@timestamp` bounds that could be moved to a control
window — exactly the no-control condition the environment notes describe for
change-mgmt lookups. No field in these payloads (key, summary, status, labels,
comments) is populated in either direction, so there is nothing to diff, and per the
rules such lookup systems are tagged state-only regardless of row content.

l-005.evidence: Observed seq 0/1/2/6 carry 31 `org.keycloak.events` LOGIN_ERROR rows between 06:13:33.104Z and 06:47:20.670Z — 30 for username `dev.dana` / client_id `admin-cli` in six ~7-second bursts from 06:46:51 to 06:47:20, plus one `smoke.test` at 06:13:33 — while all three live controls (C-21d/C-28d/C-35d) return row_count 0 for the same queries; seq 7 confirms those control windows were measured and non-empty (4–5 rows of `org.keycloak.events.jpa.JpaEventStoreProvider`), so the zeros are real absence, not a dead stack. The distinguishing fields are `username` and `client_id` (dev.dana/admin-cli) and the LOGIN_ERROR counts, none of which are on the unstable-identifier list; ip_address 172.18.0.6 alone would not have counted. Queries disagree: seq 3 and seq 4 (successful LOGIN by ip/user/client, both the 06:55 and widened 07:00 bound) return row_count 0 in observed and in every control, i.e. `absent` — there is no successful-login half of the stuffing signature, and seq 0 records logins=0, logouts=0, refresh_tokens=0. Seq 7 additionally shows ten extra loggerName values in observed (io.quarkus, infinispan, exportimport) against a single logger in baseline, consistent with a stack start inside the window.

l-006.evidence:
The rule-summary query (seq 3, untruncated on both sides) returns exactly the same 11
falco.rule values in the observed window as live control C-21d — Unexpected UDP Traffic,
BPF Program Not Profiled, Redirect STDOUT/STDIN, Launch Ingress Remote File Copy, Launch
Suspicious Network Tool, Read sensitive file untrusted, Drop and execute new binary, Read
environment variable from /proc files, Launch Sensitive Mount Container, Launch Package
Management Process, User mgmt binaries — with no cron, write-below-etc, or authorized-keys
rule in either; the targeted seq 2 query returns only the same two rules (Read sensitive
file untrusted, Launch Sensitive Mount Container) that C-21d and C-35d return. In the
untruncated seq 1 payloads every (rule, proc, parent) tuple observed (e.g. Drop and
execute/openssl/sh, Launch Suspicious Network Tool/nc/runuser, Ingress/curl/runuser) also
appears in C-21d; the only columns that differ are falco.output_fields.container.id
groupings, which environment_notes lists as regenerated per lever-up and therefore not a
delta. Counts differ in both directions against 60-minute controls versus a ~23-minute
observed span (Read sensitive file untrusted 54 vs 9/0/36; Redirect 132 vs 386/394/380;
Launch Suspicious Network Tool 58 vs 245/202/278), but the baselines themselves swing by
more than that, and no surfaced categorical field carries a value the controls lack.
